reason: The hypothesis proposes a BCC high-entropy alloy based on ZrB2, but the cited evidence describes either BCC refractory HEAs without boron (E3, E4) or HCP high-entropy diboride ceramics (E1, E2). No evidence supports the formation of a single-phase BCC structure in a ZrB2-based system with added refractory metals, nor does any evidence address the claimed improvements in oxidation durability and liquid-metal corrosion resistance for such a material. The key premise of a BCC alloy from ZrB2 is unsupported and appears to misrepresent the cited boride studies.
premises: Refractory high-entropy alloys can form a single-phase BCC structure with uniform element distribution
A single-phase BCC refractory HEA can be processed by lower-temperature techniques such as selective laser melting
Refractory HEAs exhibit excellent mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance
High-entropy boride ceramics can be synthesized as single-phase HCP structures with uniform element distribution at temperatures around 1800 °C
The addition of refractory elements to ZrB2 will yield a single-phase BCC high-entropy alloy
